When the Greeks heard that Diogenes had been captured,
they appointed Michael, the son of Constantine, as their emperor.
He seized his mother,
who was the wife of Diogenes,
and forcibly confined her in a convent.
His uncle John became his Caesar.
But when Diogenes entered Roman territory,
and heard what had happened,
he went up to the fortress of Dokeia.
There he found two hundred thousand dinars,
and sent them to the sultan with those two emirs who had accompanied him,
and informed him of the affair.
He put on the monastic habit,
and remained in Dokeia.
He sent word to Michael, saying:
“Until now I have fought the good fight on behalf of the Christian faith {OCR?},
and that is enough for me.
As for you, blessed be your reign!
You have done well to become emperor,
for it was rightfully yours.
But in good faith I advise you not to break the peace which I made with the sultan;
otherwise there will be no peace,
either for you
or for the Christians.”
Michael acknowledged his kindness and said:
“I will not depart from your counsel.”
But after some days certain men stirred him up,
and he sent word to Diogenes, saying:
“If you are truly a monk,
why do you need a residence in a fortress? You ought to go down to one of the monasteries,
so that we may send guards into the fortress.”
Diogenes became angry and said:
“Out of the whole Roman Empire, he will not leave me even one fortress!”
He rose and took off his woolen garments,
and took the merchandise of the merchants of Dokeia by way of a loan,
and gathered an army.
When the son of Sennacherib, the patrician of Lesser Armenia, came to him,
he seized him and gouged out his eyes,
and took from him eighty centenaria of gold.
He became very powerful and came to Melitene,
and sent word to Sultan Alp Arslan,
asking him for help.
The sultan promised him
that he would go in person to help him wherever circumstances required.
After this,
Diogenes moved from Melitene to Cilicia.
John marched against him,
and overpowered him in the city of Adana.
When he had captured him,
he sent word to inform Emperor Michael.
